item.title: Kitchen Renovation Side by Side

turns.text: Put these kitchen photos side by side in one landscape 16:9 image. Old kitchen on the left, renovated one on the right, labeled “Before” and “After”. Keep both photos as they are, just fit them neatly.

item.tests: Composes two supplied photos into one correctly ordered, clearly labeled comparison without regenerating either scene.

answer_sheet.Which photo goes where?: kitchen-before.jpg on the left; kitchen-after.jpg on the right.
answer_sheet.Label wording and language: Before and After, exactly, in English.
answer_sheet.Size and format: One landscape 16:9 image; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Layout and styling: Equal-sized panels with readable labels; font, colors and spacing are your call.
answer_sheet.Photo edits: Do not change either scene. Fit the complete photos without stretching; padding is fine.

must_haves: One finished 16:9 image contains both supplied kitchen photos side by side.
The brown-cabinet kitchen is on the left and the white-cabinet renovated kitchen is on the right.
The left panel is labeled exactly 'Before' and the right panel exactly 'After', with readable, unclipped text.
Both complete photos remain visible without stretching or changes to their contents.

turns.text: Put these two kitchen photos side by side in one landscape 16:9 image: the old kitchen pic on the left and the renovated kitchen pic on the right, labeled “Before” and “After”. Keep both photos as they are, just fit them neatly. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do this?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t run anything or spent any credits.**

For this layout, a **non-AI collage is the cheapest and most faithful option**: it can preserve both photos without regenerating kitchen details.

| Option | Cost | Trade-off |
|---|---:|---|
| Manual collage in a free editor such as Canva or Google Slides | **0 Magic Hour credits** | Keeps the photos unchanged apart from resizing |
| Magic Hour’s lowest-cost suitable AI edit: Flux 2 Klein, one image at 640px | **Listed from 5 credits** | AI may alter details; I can’t verify the final charge or your balance with the available tools |

**Recommended layout:** a 16:9 canvas, old kitchen on the left, renovated kitchen on the right, with “Before” and “After” above them. Fit each entire photo inside its half without cropping or stretching, using neutral padding.

A **640 × 360** collage is the smaller option; **1280 × 720** gives you more room. Making an AI request “shorter” doesn’t reduce image costs, and 640px is already the smallest listed free-plan AI setting.

I don’t have a non-AI collage tool available here. Given your requirement to keep the photos exactly as they are, I recommend the **zero-credit manual layout**, rather than spending credits on AI.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

turns.agent:
The cheapest option was the **zero-credit manual collage**. I can’t assemble it directly with the connected tools, so **I haven’t run a generation or spent any credits**.

To make it free in Canva:
1. Create a **1280 × 720 px** design.
2. Upload both kitchen photos.
3. Place the old kitchen on the **left** and the renovated one on the **right**.
4. Resize each proportionally to fit its half—**no cropping or stretching**.
5. Add **“Before”** and **“After”** above the respective photos, then download as PNG.

This preserves the original photo content. I won’t substitute the credit-costing AI option without your approval.
